slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 49:10: The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes and the allegiance of the nations is his.
slides.body: “The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes and the allegiance of the nations is his.”
slides.heading: Gen 49:10

slides.alt_text: Slide 2: Was Jesus promised through Judah? Jacob says the royal sceptre belongs to Judah. Luke later lists Judah among Jesus’s ancestors.
slides.body: Jacob says the royal sceptre belongs to Judah. Luke later lists Judah among Jesus’s ancestors.
slides.heading: Was Jesus promised through Judah?

slides.alt_text: Slide 3: Why Christians connect them The blessing points toward a ruler from Judah, and some early Jewish readers understood it as a promise about a future king. Jesus comes from the right family.
slides.body: The blessing points toward a ruler from Judah, and some early Jewish readers understood it as a promise about a future king. Jesus comes from the right family.
slides.heading: Why Christians connect them

slides.alt_text: Slide 4: But the family is enormous Judah has many descendants. Genesis does not predict one particular birth, and Luke never says Jesus fulfils this verse. The ancestry fits, but it cannot identify him by itself.
slides.body: Judah has many descendants. Genesis does not predict one particular birth, and Luke never says Jesus fulfils this verse. The ancestry fits, but it cannot identify him by itself.
slides.heading: But the family is enormous

title: Does Judahite ancestry identify the Messiah?
